title: Cyber insurance claims - what policies actually cover
p1:
Many businesses buy cyber insurance and assume they are covered the moment a hacker appears.

The reality? The biggest surprises often happen after the attack, when companies discover what their policy does and does not pay for.
p2:
A common misconception is that cyber insurance only covers data breaches.

In many cases, policies can also help with costs like ransomware response, legal support, customer notification, restoring systems, and lost income caused by a cyber incident.

But coverage depends heavily on the exact policy wording, limits, and exclusions.
p3:
One thing many leaders miss: some policies may not cover every dollar lost from a cyber event if security requirements were not followed before the attack.

The practical takeaway is simple: do not wait for a claim to learn what you bought. Review your coverage, understand exclusions, and make sure your security practices match your policy requirements.
